messages.subject: Multi-Season camera operability matrix set up
messages.subject_clean: Multi-Season camera operability matrix set up
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to create a multi-season camera operability matrix and I had a question about formatting.
I had cameras out for multiple years that were rotated between stations every 30 days approximately.

Should each row in the matrix be a separate deployment (of ~30days)?
e.g.

OR should each row correspond to one station and I create multiple problem_from & problem_to columns for each period where a camera was not at that station?
e.g.

Also, if I had a camera out from say Dec 2019 to february 2020, would it make more sense to list the session as 2019 or 2020?

Thank you!!

messages.subject: Re: Multi-Season camera operability matrix set up
messages.subject_clean: Multi-Season camera operability matrix set up
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
the first option is the suggested method, as is demonstrated in the example given in ?camtrapsMultiSeason. I'd suggest sticking with that. So even if the exact same locations are visited in multiple seasons, they should be separate rows.

The problem with the second suggested method is that you'll end up with many problem columns, can't uniquely assign a deployment to a season, and it would not allow site covariates to change between seasons.

Regarding the last question, this is really a study design question, no so much one of data management. But it sounds like the season you describe would be most adequately described as "Winter 2019", so in that case I would not split it by calendar year, but consider those three months as one season. But it really depends on the way the data were collected and how it relates to the assumtions of a multi-season model. That should be the main criterion for making this decision, and it is not really possible to give a general answer.

Please also see vignette 3 for a demonstration of the workflow for multi-season occupancy models.
Best regards,
Jürgen

My code

                 legendPosition = "topleft",

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] activityOverlap plot legend size
messages.body_plain:
Hi Raquel,
this is currently not directly possible. While you can pass additional arguments to activityOverlap() in "...", these are passed to overlapPlot(), which in turn passes them to plot(). That doesn't help with the legend, which is created independentlyof plot() with legend().

Here are a few potential workarounds:
increase pngWidth and pngHeight
in the RStudio plot window, change the size of the window and it will change the look of the figure also. Then export from there.
modify the code of the function here <https://github.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/blob/master/R/activityOverlap.R>, around line 227 and/or 254.
use the output of activityOverlap (a data frame with time and density values of both species) and make your own plot in base R or ggplot2, with full control over the legend
In the long run I'd like to port these function to ggplot if I find the time, but haven't yet managed to.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: recordTable() failed to extract metadata
messages.body_plain:
Jürgen

My usual call on recordTable failed.
Images from other cameras captured at the same time worked as expected.
Usually, I process multiple camera stations from one or more 'projects' hence the inDir argument.  This call work for all but one camera-station.

            recordTable(inDir = paste (image_directory, projects[ iproj], sep = "") ,
                        IDfrom = "directory",
                        timeZone = "Etc/GMT-10",
                        removeDuplicateRecords = FALSE,
                        additionalMetadataTags =
                            c( # "EXIF:CameraModelName",
                              "MakerNotes:SerialNumber",
                              "MakerNotes:UserLabel",
                              "MakerNotes:AmbientTemperature",
                              "MakerNotes:MoonPhase",
                              "MakerNotes:BatteryVoltage",
#                              "MakerNotes:TriggerMode",
                              "MakerNotes:Sequence",
                              "MakerNotes:EventNumber",
#                             "MakerNotes:MotionSensitivity",
#                              "MakerNotes:FirmwareVersion",
                              "EXIF:ExifImageHeight",
                               #  "EXIF:SceneCaptureType",
                              "XMP:Subject",
                              "IPTC:Keywords"))

Error: something went wrong. I looked through all those 1 folders
and now your table is empty. Were date/time information unreadable?
Could species tags not be extracted (if IDfrom = 'metadata')?
Or did you exclude too many species?

When I look at the metadata using the app "exifPro" the data time metadata are missing.
When I use exiftool all the metadata are present and correct.

However, the firmware on my Reconyx is v old, 2010.

I am using
This is camtrapR 2.1.0 (DEVELOPMENT)
I think I am using a recent version exiftool - see screen shot.
How do I ask exiftool for its version?
I downloaded and installed a new copy of exiftool today and from the terminal successfully extracted all the metadata.

So why is my combination of images/camtrapR/exiftool failing to read the metadata for this single station. Ah - perhaps the date time is in the wrong format in this old version of the firmware?

David

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] recordTable() failed to extract metadata
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,
I can't tell what's wrong without a sample image. Would you mind sharing one please?

It is possible that the camera model did not save the date/time tags correctly - some models are known to have this problem.

Normally exiftool doesn't cause problems, and even old versions normally work just fine. I don't think I've had any real problems with exiftool. In Windows the version is accessible with right-click > Details. Don't know about Mac.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Difference between metadata values of an image and timestamp noted on the image
messages.subject_clean: Difference between metadata values of an image and timestamp noted on the image
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am currently working on a camera trap dataset and I have extracted all data using the recordTable function. Then I used R to select the snapshot moment every 2 seconds. But when I checked the images that were selected as snapshot moments (so where time finishes by an even number), I noticed that the metadata extracted by Exiftool and camtrapR for the time was sometimes slightly different from the timestamp written directly on the image. Here is an example to make things clearer.

Image 03080345.JPG

Timestamp noted on the image : 09:26:53
Timestamp extracted usding Exiftool and CamtrapR (record table): 09:26:54

There therefore seems to be a difference a 1 second (sometimes no difference, less frequently a difference of 2 seconds) between the metadata of the image and the timestamp on the image. It appears that the metadata corresponding to the date and time is slightly different, maybe because it corresponds to the time the file was created.

I am trying to see if it is an error on my side or if it already happened to other people, and also if it will have an impact if I am working on metadata values (and not timestamp on the image) to extract snapshop moment.

Thank you for you help and don't hesitate if you would like more information or to see my data.

Best regards,

Emeline Auda

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] recordTable() failed to extract metadata
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,

I tested it and recordTable worked without problems after running fixDateTimeOriginal first.

Note however that I did not use the "~/Desktop" path notation, used an absolute path instead. Personally I prefer giving absolute paths, and often construct them with file.path(). That way I usually only need to change one line at the top of a script if paths change, as long as the other paths relative to the main path are constant. And the script won't rely on whatever the current working directory is.

Not sure about years old R code. Something beyond my control might have changed also during the many changes from R3.x to R4. I don't think I made any changes that would break how camtrapR handles paths.

For the record, these were Reconxy HC600 Covert cameras. This model does not store date/time correctly, and it needs to be corrected with fixDateTimeOriginal.

Btw, I discovered a bug where recordTable would assign n_images = 0 to the directories "first" and "last", both containing one image only. Fixed on github.

Best,

Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Difference between metadata values of an image and timestamp noted on the image
messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] Difference between metadata values of an image and timestamp noted on the image
messages.body_plain:
Hi Emeline,

thank you, this is interesting and I haven't seen this before.

I suspect there is some sort of delay during image processing in the camera, which leads to the time difference. Maybe the camera system queries the internal time twice: once when writing the data field in the image, and again later when writing the EXIF metadata. That would be beyond my control, but it's just speculation.

There's not a lot we can do here. Personally I'd just go with the metadata, since they are easy to read out without error. Even if they are a second late. For very time-critical applications a different camera model might be more suitable though.

The alternative would be to use optical character recognition to extract the time from the data field in the images, but that is not very reliable unfortunately and may misread the numbers and requires checking. See ?OCRdataFields.

Best regards,

Jürgen
